> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 33 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee88a3ac1aee62f302a361e60553113de54fc68a` — the merge of head `75b4c850fa3d6eec9790f37ccbb422edfc5eca38` into base `efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee88a3ac1aee62f302a361e60553113de54fc68a && git checkout ee88a3ac1aee62f302a361e60553113de54fc68a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815 75b4c850fa3d6eec9790f37ccbb422edfc5eca38 && git checkout -B drift-repro efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815 && git merge --no-ff 75b4c850fa3d6eec9790f37ccbb422edfc5eca38

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75b4c850fa3d6eec9790f37ccbb422edfc5eca38`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #15206's triage unlock 6107774330, the claim 6108222334, the os-dev-reports 6108953446 (round 1) and 6109357048 (round 2); S5's ACCEPT 6097795222 and contract review 6097501912 for what was carried; card #22835's body; PR #22833 (its body, its 6-file list, and the net diff against the merge base `b7cd1af9df`: 6 files, +153 / −34, equal to the file list, over the four branch commits `e4cb38f3fd`, `baaa75e036`, `1fec8e5dd0`, `75b4c850fa`); PR #22776's merged diff (`60bcfe726c`, an ancestor of the merge base) where it touches the permission-set fork's disposition — its changeset, its `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` hunk and its `protocol.ts` hunk; the 42 check-runs and the one commit status on the head, read at 2026-10-11T13:25Z; `git merge-tree` of the head against `origin/main` at `1eff3224d7`. Source at the head, read by symbol: `protocol.ts` (`isSealedManagedItem`, `isArtifactBacked`, `registryAllowsOverlay`, `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES`, `mergesOverlayAtRead`, `isDeclaredCodeDatasource`, `isHostCodeDatasource`, `declinesStoredRow`, `isUnservedSealedOverlay`, `refusePackagedBaseRemoval`, `loadMetaFromDb`, `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows`, `reportSealedOverlayRows`, the protocol's and `SysMetadataRepository`'s `listDrafts`, `packageScopedRowWhere`), `permission-set-projection.ts` (`projectPermissionMutation`), `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` (`restoreRuntimeDatasources`, `loadDatasourceRows`), objectql's `plugin.ts` (`refuseEnvironmentHeldSecurityCatalogNames`), the cli's `migrate/security-catalog-overlays`, the two package entries and `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`; the same symbols at `c8b062f011^` for each FROM side; on `main`: `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`'s header, `pr-automation.yml` and `lint.yml` where they run it, and the fleet's landing rule. ⛔ Not the dispatch order, not the dispatching seat's conclusions. Nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run; the dev's `dispatch-gates` run is read as the dev's report, never as a gate verdict. This is a `security` card: classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head, as read.** 42 check-runs, all `completed`, none in progress: 36 `success`, 4 `skipped`, 2 `failure`. Every one of the seven required contexts is `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (and its four `Type Check ·` legs), `Test Core` (and its six shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (rollup and 1/3 to 3/3), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also green: `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter`, `Auto Label`, and the four claim and closing guards, twice each — `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` among them. Skipped by contract: `Console Pin Gate` (path filter; the pin is unchanged), `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and the second run's `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` twins (the `edited` event after the round-2 body write). **Red: `Check Changeset`, twice** — 114469951637 on the push run and 114477462305 on the `edited` run, the latter completed 2026-10-11T13:09:17Z — attributed in ③. The one commit status, `Vercel`, is `success` ("Canceled by Ignored Build Step"). Not governed: no path under `.claude/`, `docs/adr/`, `skills/`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; head repo is the base repo; 187 changed lines over 6 files, under every threshold; draft, `auto_merge` unset, no `skip-changeset` label (right — ruling D on #18375 refuses it for this class), `mergeable: true` with `mergeable_state: unstable` (the red advisory check, not a conflict).

1. **Per-term isolation in `[metadata_org_scoped_unserved]`** (`reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows`). On the merge base one `try` held the projected `sys_metadata` find and the three `engine.count` ledger reads; any failure other than a missing table left the function through its outer empty `catch` and the line was never printed. At the head each of the four reads runs inside `isolated(object, read)`, whose `catch` appends `object (message)` to `unmeasured`; the early return now requires `rows`, `ledgers` and `unmeasured` all empty; and the line gains one clause, `NOT MEASURED, so this account may be incomplete — the read failed: …`, after the measured terms. RIGHT: a failing read prints NOT MEASURED with its reason and never a zero — a failed ledger pushes nothing to `ledgers` (only a positive count is ever pushed, and no count exists for it), a failed `sys_metadata` read leaves `rows` empty so the per-type clause is omitted rather than printed as `×0`; the missing-table arm is untouched (`orNoTable` still asks `isMissingTableError` and returns the empty value — an unprovisioned ledger still reads as zero, by design); the boot verdict is unchanged — `storeUnavailable` is set only in `loadMetaFromDb`'s own catch, which this diagnostic's own `try`/`catch` never reaches, and the diff does not touch that site. Pinned: the new cold-boot case (history count throws → `flow×1 (org_sweep@org_a)`, `sys_metadata_commit×1, sys_metadata_audit×1`, `NOT MEASURED`, `sys_metadata_history (history count refused)`, and no `sys_metadata_history×` term), and the existing failing-probe case re-premised from "no line" to "one line naming `sys_metadata (probe exploded)`", with its `storeUnavailable: false` / `errors: 0` assertions kept; the dev's ablation (the per-term catch made to rethrow: 2 red) is the recorded direction; `Test Core` is green. The `sys_metadata` term the dev added beyond the three ledgers the hypothesis named is the same failure shape and the right reading of "per-ledger". Cosmetic, not a ground: when NOT MEASURED is the only clause, the closing sentence's "carries these rows" names no row.

2. **The host-code-datasource leave-out** (`isHostCodeDatasource`, `loadMetaFromDb`). The new private predicate is exactly the first half of `isDeclaredCodeDatasource` — the kernel service `code-datasource-names`, the set the datasource-admin restore reads (`codeDatasourceNamesOf(ctx)` in `restoreRuntimeDatasources`) — and `isDeclaredCodeDatasource` now reads that half through it (one reading; the type check it repeats is redundant and harmless), so its answer is unchanged. In `loadMetaFromDb` the exclusion sits inside the `isUnservedSealedOverlay` branch: a sealed row whose name is in the host set is no longer pushed to `sealedOverlays`, while the `object` skip and the hydration that follows are untouched, so what boot loads does not move. RIGHT on the three counts the brief asks: (i) every read still declines both kinds — `declinesStoredRow` is unchanged in code and still answers `isDeclaredCodeDatasource(type, name) || isUnservedSealedOverlay(type, name)`, true for a host-set name and for a manifest-declared one; (ii) manifest-only names stay listed — the package-manifest half lives only in `isDeclaredCodeDatasource`, so `isHostCodeDatasource` is false for them and the push happens; (iii) the row IS named once, by `restoreRuntimeDatasources`' warning (`datasource restore: sys_metadata holds a stored row for '…', a datasource this host defines in code … Remove it with DELETE /api/v1/meta/datasource/…`), which fires on exactly `codeNames.has(name)` — the same set. Pinned: the new `reads-environment-only` case (host set `host_ds`, manifest `pkg_ds`: both `declinesStoredRow` true; the sealed line names `datasource×1 (pkg_ds)` and not `host_ds`); the dev's real boot through `bootShowcase` (named twice on `baaa75e036`, once on `1fec8e5dd0`). The stated limit holds and is the ruling's cost (③): a host that composes no `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` names such a row nowhere at boot — `os serve` (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`) and the verify harness both compose it, so the shipped compositions are covered.

3. **The TSDoc against the code.** `isSealedManagedItem` at the head is `isArtifactBacked(type, name) && !registryAllowsOverlay(type)`; `registryAllowsOverlay` reads `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES`, built from `allowOrgOverride` on `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`, which has exactly five such entries (`view`, `dashboard`, `report`, `translation`, `email_template`); `isUnservedSealedOverlay` is false for `permission` and otherwise `isSealedManagedItem`; `refusePackagedBaseRemoval` refuses when `isSealedManagedItem` holds and `mergesOverlayAtRead(type)` does not, and `mergesOverlayAtRead` reads the `supportsOverlay` set (`permission`, `position`, `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `book`, `tool`, `skill`, plus the five above). Judged line by line: `declinesStoredRow` — "ANY type whose registry entry opens no overlay channel … every type but the five regime-O ones, so a merge-at-read `page` or `app` as much as a flow or an object, `permission` excepted" is the predicate's reach, RIGHT; `reportSealedOverlayRows` — "which stored ENVIRONMENT rows no read serves" (not "boot did not load", which held for `object` alone), the same reach, "an `object` such row is not even loaded", and the host-datasource sentence — each true at the head, RIGHT; `refusePackagedBaseRemoval` — "removing a row of a type that merges at read removes no managed definition. Only for `permission`, whose stored fork is still served, does it change what is served; every other such row is served by no read already" — true: among the sealed merge-at-read types, `permission` is the one `isUnservedSealedOverlay` excepts, so its fork is served and its removal changes the answer; every other is declined at read, RIGHT; `isSealedManagedItem` — the carve-out "removes no managed definition (and changes what is served for `permission` alone)" replaces "restores the managed definition", the same correction, RIGHT. The `isUnservedSealedOverlay` paragraph #22776 wrote is byte-untouched in the diff. Comments only; nothing executable moves.

4. **The two FROM → TO rows, by symbol.** Row `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` row `organizationId` (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`): at `c8b062f011^` the repository's `listDrafts` returned `organizationId: string | null` on every row and read `packageScopedRowWhere(this.organizationId, 'draft', filter)` (an `$or` of the instance's organization and `null`); at the head the row type has no `organizationId` and the read is `packageScopedRowWhere('draft', filter)`, which is `state: 'draft'` plus `organization_id: null` plus the filter — "every listed row is an environment draft, whichever repository asks" is the code's own comment and true for a `legacyOrganizationRepo(id)` instance too. `SysMetadataRepository` is an entry export of the package, so the narrowing is published; RIGHT. Row `organizationId` on `projectPermissionMutation`'s `evt` (`@objectstack/plugin-security`): at `c8b062f011^` the `evt` type carried `organizationId?: string | null` and forwarded it into `getMetaItemLayered`; at the head the type has `type`, `name`, `state` only and the layered read is `{ type: 'permission', name: evt.name }` — "the projection reads the environment → code layered read, whatever organization the event names" is true at runtime (the handler passes `evt: any`; the key is ignored). `projectPermissionMutation` is an entry export; RIGHT. Both are the two narrowings 6097501912 ② named and 6097795222 carried; 6107774330 orders them before the v18 release.

5. **The `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` sentence.** "A row under the name of a datasource the host defines in code is named once, by the datasource restore's boot warning, with that warning's remedy." True at the head for every composition that carries the restore (item 2), and needed: the paragraph's "Boot names each such row, per type (`[metadata_sealed_overlay_unserved]`)" became false for exactly that row on `1fec8e5dd0`. The permission sentence that follows is #22776's and untouched. RIGHT. A hand-written tree (`content/docs/concepts/`, not `references/` or `releases/`); `Check Documentation Links` and `Build Docs` green.

6. **The DELIBERATE CORRECTION, ① part.** The modified note is **`.changeset/15206-reads-environment-only.md`**, S5's pending v18 release note (PR #22628, `c8b062f011`, an ancestor of the merge base); it is unchanged on `origin/main` since the merge base, so what the diff rewrites is what `main` holds. Three edits against `main`, each judged:
   - **Inserted row 1** (after the `ListDraftsResponse` row): `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` row `organizationId` → gone. Not a falsity on `main` but an omission of a published narrowing S5 made; the inserted text is true at the head (item 4). RIGHT.
   - **Inserted row 2** (after the `MetadataAuthoringGateContext.organizationId` row): `organizationId` on `projectPermissionMutation`'s `evt` → drop it. Same class; true at the head (item 4). RIGHT.
   - **Rewritten sentence** (the `[Triage ruling Q1 → C]` bullet's last sentence). OLD, on `main`: "A stored fork of a code-declared permission set keeps its own ruling (detection reading and Discard Overlay) and is still served." **False on `main` because of #22776** (merged 2026-10-11T09:39:02Z, `60bcfe726c`, before this branch forked), not because of this PR: #22776 retired the Discard Overlay action, its REST route and its contract member, and its own pending note states the replacement — "a database holding one is refused at cold boot (ADR-0048)", "clear any overlay offline with `os migrate security-catalog-overlays --apply`"; #22776 also rewrote the `isUnservedSealedOverlay` paragraph and the `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` sentence to that disposition, and could not touch #15206's note without the same #17712 refusal — so the stale sentence was `main`'s, and it would have published a retired action as this release's disposition. NEW: "keeps its own ruling instead: the reads do not decline it, a cold boot refuses a deployment that holds one (ADR-0048), and the offline `os migrate security-catalog-overlays` removes it." **True at the head**: `isUnservedSealedOverlay` returns false for `permission`, so no read declines the fork (the S5 pin's "a permission fork served" case stands); `ObjectQLPlugin.refuseEnvironmentHeldSecurityCatalogNames` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`) runs right after `sys_metadata` hydrates, under ADR-0048; `os migrate security-catalog-overlays` exists in `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/` and deletes with `--apply` — "removes it" compresses the `--apply` arm, which `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` on `main` spells out beside it; a precision note, not a falsity. RIGHT, and the sentence matches #22776's changeset and the dev's round-2 report.
   - **Left untouched and named as waiting on #22835**: the first "What changes" bullet's "A row stored organization-scoped by an earlier release is served by no read and loaded by no boot", and the boot line's "no read serves them, boot does not load them" — the latter is the `[metadata_org_scoped_unserved]` text in `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows` (`protocol.ts`), not a changeset sentence. Both are false on `main` today for one type, `datasource`, by the gap the dev measured on a real boot and #22835 carries: `restoreRuntimeDatasources` → `loadDatasourceRows` reads `sys_metadata` by type and state with no organization predicate, so a legacy organization-scoped `datasource` row is registered and served while the line names it as unserved. **Correctly left**: this PR did not make them false (they have been false since S5 landed), rewriting them would publish a known gap as the v18 contract, and #22835 is `target:v18` with "must land before the release that ships" this note — which makes #22835 a condition of the note's truth, flagged in ③ for the release board, not a ground against this diff.
   - **Anything else in the note now false?** One clause is narrowed by this PR, not falsified: "`[metadata_sealed_overlay_unserved]` lists the sealed overlays per type with the two remedies" — after item 2 it lists all but the host-code-datasource subclass, which the restore names with its one remedy; the new patch note `.changeset/15206-boot-report-carry-overs.md` states that carve-out in the same release, and "Boot names both populations, once each" stays true. The FROM → TO row for "an environment overlay of a managed item on a sealed type (flow, action, hook, object, datasource …)" keeps both its remedies for that row. Every other sentence — frontmatter, title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 marker, the reads list, `overlayScope`, `listDrafts`, `listCommits`, the objectql binders, the form doors, the seed loader, the other table rows, "What does not change" — is unchanged in the diff and unchanged in truth by it. The dev's "every other line of that note is unchanged" is what the diff shows (+3 / −1 on that file).

**Nothing is deleted or rewritten.** No added line calls a store write; the two reads the diff wraps are the same `find` and `count` with the same `where`, `fields` and system context.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15206-boot-report-carry-overs.md` (new, this PR's own — an `A` row, outside the foreign rule): `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, two bullets naming items 1 and 2. The level is right: a behaviour change in a released package — the boot log's content (one clause gained on the legacy line; one subclass of row leaving the sealed line) — with no public type, request, response, enum, export or error code moving: `isHostCodeDatasource` and `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows` are private, `declinesStoredRow` changes in TSDoc only, and `SysMetadataRepository` and the plugin-security entry are untouched in code (their rows above describe S5's narrowing, already bumped `minor` by the pending note). `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` are not in the file list and owe nothing. Nothing published moves in shape; what moves is observable boot output, which is what a `patch` is for and what the Post-Task Checklist refuses `skip-changeset` for. The pending note's frontmatter (six packages, `minor`, the ADR-0087 marker) is untouched by the diff, so the correction changes no level. `Clause-②: no` on PR body line 2, in the new changeset and in the claim 6108222334 — matches the diff: no read refused today is admitted, no accept set widens or narrows; the one membership change is a boot report's, not a door's. Not a `(narrowing)`: no caller loses an answer. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags
